idea: WEV Jevifies any local model, for free: see inside it, give it a typed decision mode, calibrate it, and gate it. (1) Inspect: a glass-box view of the model's next-token probabilities and entropy. (2) Jevify: you define a typed decision (choice, score or yes/no over a closed label set) and decide() answers it in one pass with per-label probabilities and a confidence, while generate() keeps the model's normal abilities. (3) Calibrate: WEV measures on real examples whether that confidence can be trusted. (4) Gate: confident decisions are acted on, uncertain ones fall back to the model's own generate() or a human. (5) Export: the wrapper, gate card and tests copy into your app as code, and every decision has a hashed receipt that /verify re-checks. Works with in-browser ONNX causal LMs via transformers.js, a local OpenAI-compatible server that returns token log-probs (experimental), or pre-scored output files from any model; no server and no API key needed. An optional reference model can audit the labels; the gate never depends on it.

wedge.title: wev
wedge.sector: WEB2 · Reliability tooling for on-device LLM features
wedge.target_user: A developer adding a small on-device LLM feature (autocomplete, form-fill, classification) who must decide, per output, whether to act on it or fall back to a default or a human
wedge.painful_moment: The model always returns an answer, even when its top two candidates were nearly tied or its distribution was flat. The developer has no per-output signal for 'safe to act on', so either everything is trusted or everything is double-checked.
wedge.unusual_constraint: Any local model in the supported set (ONNX causal LMs in the browser, a local log-prob server, or pre-scored files) becomes a typed System 1 decider with a measured confidence, entirely on the user's machine: no server, no API key needed, and no second model grading the first at runtime. The only hosted model in the repo is an optional reference labeller used by pnpm reference, and the gate never reads its labels.
wedge.proof_metric: TARGET (unmeasured until `pnpm capture && pnpm calibrate` run): on a held-out half of ~100 synthetic labelled items, auto-handling only CONFIDENT verdicts gives higher accuracy than always taking the model's answer, reported as accuracy at coverage. Publish whatever the numbers are.
wedge.essential_sponsor_role: No sponsor is integrated. Inference stays local so the demo needs no key.

adversarial_critique.why_generic_risk: Token-probability viewers are common. WEV's difference is the decision on top: act, flag, or refuse, with a measured accuracy-at-coverage number instead of a picture.
adversarial_critique.obvious_competitor: Purpose-trained System 1 models such as Jev (TypeSafe AI) that return typed values and confidence out of the box, and generic transformers.js / LM visualizers. WEV is not a model: it adapts the models people already run, then measures whether their confidence can be trusted.
adversarial_critique.unprovable_claim_risk: A general LLM wrapped as a decider is an approximation, not equal to a model trained for typed decisions, and its confidence may be poorly calibrated. Labelled items are synthetic and builder-written. State item count, split, model and task wherever a number appears. Do not claim Jev compatibility or equivalence unless tested against real Jev output. The reference model is a second labeller, so agreement with it is not accuracy against truth.
adversarial_critique.hour_8_kill_criterion: If the gate does not beat 'always take the model's answer' on the held-out half, show that on /proof as an honest negative result and lead the demo with the failure gallery.

reasons: Crowded space (token viewers). Differentiator is the measured act-or-abstain gate; moat score from the old heuristic search was dropped as stale.
angles: Accuracy at coverage on captured real-model runs, reproducible with one command
Fails closed: malformed or flat distributions are escalated, never shown as confident
Decision receipts: every auto-action is replayable and tamper-evident

features.feature: Capture ~100 real SmolLM2 runs on a closed-label task; replace hand-written fixtures; seeded 50/50 split
features.why: Every number on screen becomes measured

features.feature: Decider spec: define a typed decision (kind choice|score|noul, closed label set, instruction and few-shot examples). WEV scores every label's FULL token sequence in one pass (not just first token) and returns {value, probabilities, confidence} against a JSON schema; thresholds read from evidence/thresholds.json
features.why: This is the 'Jev-style for any model' step and removes the top-5 renormalization distortion

features.feature: Model adapters behind one interface: in-browser transformers.js logits; local server with token log-probabilities (Ollama or llama.cpp, experimental); import of pre-scored outputs (text, gold, predicted, confidence or per-label probabilities) from any model
features.why: Lets many models be Jev-style without WEV running them

features.feature: Dual-mode wrapper: jevify(model) returns { decide(), generate() }. decide() is the calibrated System 1 path; generate() is the model's unchanged normal behaviour. The gate routes low-confidence decisions to generate() (System 2 fallback) or the human queue, and the inbox shows which path each item took
features.why: Shows the model keeps its abilities and gains Jev-style decisions, and makes the System 1 to System 2 handoff real

features.feature: Live inbox: items stream through the model; auto-handled vs escalated counters against an always-trust baseline
features.why: Gives the demo a story and shows mistakes caught
The one convincing visual for the gate

features.feature: Exportable gate (copy as TypeScript) with generated tests drawn from the calibration set
features.why: Makes it a tool developers can use in CI

features.feature: Gate card JSON: model id, thresholds, calibration size, accuracy at coverage, date, limits
features.why: Shareable, model-card-style record of what was measured

features.feature: Decision receipts (input, probabilities, gate version, verdict, sha256) re-checked on /verify with tamper detection
features.why: Ties directly to the deterministic kernel and /proof track

features.feature: `pnpm calibrate` re-derives every on-screen number from committed captured runs with a fixed seed
features.why: Answers 'how do I know these numbers are real'

features.feature: Failure gallery and limits panel on /proof
Offline moment: load the model once, switch to airplane mode, run the inbox. Claim it only if tested
Calibrate on your own examples: paste or drop ~30 labelled items (CSV/JSON), WEV runs the chosen model on them and derives thresholds, accuracy at coverage and a gate card for that model and task
features.why: Makes WEV a tool for any local model, not a one-model demo

features.feature: Model picker with 2-3 pre-tested presets (SmolLM2-135M, SmolLM2-360M, one more) plus a custom Hugging Face ONNX model id marked experimental

EXPERIMENTAL bring-your-own-model: drop a local ONNX model folder (config, tokenizer, onnx weights) and load it through a transformers.js custom cache; clear error if the architecture, size or memory fails
features.why: Run the gate on a model that never left the user's machine

features.feature: Optional, cut first: cost-aware thresholds (cost of a wrong auto-action vs a human review), per-token uncertainty strip, prompt A/B, drift check
features.why: Extra depth only if the core is done

landing.name: WEV
landing.promise: Jevify your local model. See it, calibrate it, trust it. For free.
landing.usp: Wrap any local model, Jev-style: it keeps working, but can now decide: a typed answer with measured confidence. Confident ones run instantly; the rest fall back or escalate. Copy the wrapper into your app. No server, no key.
landing.problem: Small models always answer, even when they were guessing, and they return text, not a typed decision with a trustworthy confidence. Your app cannot tell which answers are safe to act on.
landing.boundary: Reads probabilities on your device; never sends your prompts to a server. The model downloads once (~130MB) from a CDN, then is cached.
